In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis, structural and transport properties of nanograin size proton conducting oxide materials.
the development of protonic materials for solid oxide fuel cells (SOFCs).
the structural study and proton transport properties of bulk nanograin size of 3-5 nm of Y-doped Ba ZrO3 oxide materials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the structural and transport properties of bulk nano-grained Y-doped BZO are not affected by the presence of nanograin boundaries, but the grain size is the most important factor in determining the proton conductivity of the material.
the proton transport in BZY20 bulk nanograined material is enhanced by the nanograin size effect, and the proton transport is also enhanced by the Y-dopant effect.

the proton transport in BZY is a result of a combination of protonic conduction in the bulk of the grains and the surface proton conduction on the grain boundary, and that the grain boundary conduction is dominant in the low temperature region, and the bulk conduction is dominant at high temperatures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proton conductivity of the bulk nanograin size BZY20 material is comparable to that of the nanograin size BaZr0.8Y0.2O3-δ (BZY20), which has been reported by other groups.
we are working on proton conducting materials for fuel cell applications.
the structural study and proton transport properties of nanograin size BZY20 proton conducting solid electrolytes have been studied.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the protonic conductivity in BZY is not only a function of the grain size but also the oxygen partial pressure.
the nanosized grains in the bulk of the material are the active sites for the proton transport.
the nanograin size of the BZY20 electrolyte is a crucial parameter to enhance the proton transport and the protonic conductivity of BZY20 is significantly enhanced at low temperatures.
